steps.title: Result & rank declared
steps.body: After you write NEET UG, NTA (the exam body) publishes your scorecard with your marks and an All India Rank (AIR). This rank decides which colleges you can apply to — lower rank numbers mean better options. Download your scorecard from the NTA website and keep it safe because you'll need it in every step that follows.

steps.title: Registration on counselling portal
steps.body: You need to register on the MCC (Medical Counselling Committee) website for AIQ (All India Quota) seats, or on your state's counselling portal for state quota seats — or both if you want to try for both. Registration means filling in your personal details, uploading documents, and paying a refundable security deposit. Missing the registration window means you cannot participate in that round at all, so set reminders.
documents: Class 10 certificate (for date of birth proof)

steps.title: Document verification
steps.body: After registration, your uploaded documents are verified — either online or at a designated centre depending on the counselling body. If any document is missing, incorrect, or doesn't match your registration data, your application can be rejected. Double-check every upload: make sure scans are clear, the name spelling matches across all documents, and category certificates are in the prescribed format.

steps.title: Choice filling & locking
steps.body: This is where you pick the colleges and courses you want, ranked in order of your preference. You can add as many choices as you like — there's no limit. Once you're satisfied, you 'lock' your choices. If you don't lock them yourself before the deadline, the system auto-locks whatever you last saved. Strategy matters here: putting too few choices or only dream colleges is risky, so add a healthy mix of reach, match, and safety options.

steps.title: Seat allotment (round-wise)
steps.body: MCC runs multiple rounds of allotment (usually Round 1, Round 2, and Round 3). In each round, the system looks at your rank and your preference list, then assigns you the best possible seat from your choices that's still available. After each round you can accept the seat, 'float up' (keep the seat but stay in for upgrades in the next round), or exit. If you don't get allotted in a round, you automatically stay in for the next one.

steps.title: Reporting & admission
steps.body: Once you accept a seat, you must physically report to the allotted college within the given deadline — usually 5 to 7 days. You'll submit original documents, pay the first-year tuition fee, and formally take admission. If you don't report on time, your seat is cancelled and your security deposit may be forfeited. Carry every original document along with two sets of photocopies.
steps.timing_window: Within 5–7 days of each allotment result

steps.title: Mop-up & stray vacancy rounds
steps.body: After all regular rounds, seats that weren't filled — because students didn't report, or chose a different college — become available again in 'mop-up' rounds. If still vacant after mop-up, a final 'stray vacancy' round happens where colleges directly admit from remaining candidates. These rounds are your last chance, and cutoffs here can sometimes be more relaxed than earlier rounds. Keep your documents ready even if you weren't allotted earlier.
documents: Proof of non-admission / non-reporting (if previously allotted)
